Command `bash /workspace/build.sh 'cd /gt/_work/src/test && git checkout fuzz.c && python3 -c "
with open(\"fuzz.c\", \"r\") as f:
    content = f.read()
# Add debug to print mm fields before calling mg_mqtt_next_prop
old = \"while ((ofs = mg_mqtt_next_prop(&mm, &prop, ofs)) > 0) {\"
new = \"fprintf(stderr, \\\"DEBUG: mm.dgram.buf=%p mm.dgram.len=%zu props_start=%zu props_size=%zu\\\\n\\\", mm.dgram.buf, mm.dgram.len, mm.props_start, mm.props_size);\\n      while ((ofs = mg_mqtt_next_prop(&mm, &prop, ofs)) > 0) {\"
content = content.replace(old, new)
with open(\"fuzz.c\", \"w\") as f:
    f.write(content)
print(\"Modified\")
" && cc fuzz.c -DMAIN -O1 -g -fsanitize=address -fno-omit-frame-pointer -DMG_ENABLE_SOCKET=0 -DMG_ENABLE_LOG=0 -DMG_ENABLE_LINES=1 -DMG_ENABLE_TCPIP=1 -I. -o /tmp/fuzzer_dbg6 2>&1 | tail -5 && printf "\x30\x07\x00\x01\x61\x80\x80\x80\x00" > /tmp/poc.bin && /tmp/fuzzer_dbg6 /tmp/poc.bin 2>&1 | head -20'` executed with exit code 0.

message.content:
Both files have the vulnerable code. The `prop->id = i[0]` reads before the bounds check.

Let me check if the fuzzer binary is actually using this code. Let me check if the fuzzer binary was built with the correct `mongoose.c` by checking the binary's build ID or by disassembling the `mg_mqtt_next_prop` function.

Actually, let me check if the fuzzer binary is actually calling `mg_mqtt_next_prop` with the right arguments. The debug output showed `DEBUG: calling mg_mqtt_next_prop ofs=0`. But maybe the `mm` structure is not what I think it is.

Let me add debug output inside `mg_mqtt_next_prop` to print the values of `msg->dgram.buf`, `msg->dgram.len`, `msg->props_start`, and `msg->props_size`.
